scope: Independent review of the SERVICE-001 decision candidate and its pinned local HTTP mail provider. The owner's successor decision is assumed settled: a changed due date after an accepted reminder calls for a new reminder with a fresh durable intent ID, stable across attempts and reconciliation.

findings.finding: Every reviewed artifact still uses Todo.id for provider deduplication. A second reminder for the same Todo with a changed due_at reuses the key with a changed payload and the pinned provider returns 409. The owner's accepted successor cannot be frozen with these artifacts unchanged.
findings.required_successor: Retain the original source and its digest as comparison evidence. Add a reviewed successor with a generated UUID delivery-intent ID persisted before HTTP dispatch. Bind the intent to Todo ID, due-date schedule revision and immutable request payload. Use that same ID in the body and Idempotency-Key header for every attempt and reconciliation; never derive it from an attempt, worker lease or Todo ID. Change the JOB-001 successor expectation to the persisted intent ID, and add a completed A -> due-date patch -> eligible B -> second 202 trace with distinct keys.

findings.finding: The source maps all provider timeouts to a retryable application failure, while a request that may have been dispatched is OutcomeUnknown and must not be blindly retried. The plan recognizes the conflict but has no revised declaration or checked positive/negative fixture yet.
findings.required_successor: Distinguish proved pre-dispatch refusal or timeout from any timeout, connection loss, malformed acknowledgement or unexpected response after possible dispatch. Only the former can be retryable. Persist an inspectable unknown outcome under the same intent identity; no scheduled restart or lease expiry may send again without trustworthy reconciliation. Include a negative fixture rejecting the blanket timeout mapping.

findings.finding: The post-send write checks only Todo.id and reminder_sent_at == none. If the due date changes after A is selected but before A's receipt is stored, A can mark the new B schedule as sent without delivering B. A repeated scan can also create distinct intents for the same schedule unless intent creation is unique and transactional.
findings.required_successor: Create at most one active intent for a Todo schedule revision using a transaction and uniqueness guard. Before dispatch, check eligibility and that the intent still names the current schedule; after a valid receipt, mark Todo.reminder_sent_at only if the same revision remains current. Preserve A's accepted or unknown outcome in its intent record even when B supersedes it. Add interleaving fixtures for patch before dispatch, patch after dispatch before acknowledgement, and two workers selecting B.

findings.finding: The exact-byte OpenAPI pin and closed operation are sound, but the reviewed declaration does not yet explicitly bind the bearer security scheme to an Authorization header or require request body idempotency_key to equal the header key. The reference provider's same-key/same-payload semantics depend on that equality and a fixed payload.
findings.required_successor: Freeze the credential sink as Authorization: Bearer with the config.mail_api_key value hidden from authored code, fakes, logs and errors. Validate body/header identity equality before dispatch and response/header identity equality before constructing a receipt. Keep the exact host, port, path, method, no-proxy and no-redirect checks and the existing immutable OpenAPI version/hash; document that the import is review data, not execution authority.

findings.finding: The OpenAPI contract offers POST only and no status lookup. A lost 202 response therefore cannot be automatically resolved by a provider lookup under this pinned operation. The plan's phrase 'receipt or provider status lookup' is broader than the actual snapshot.
findings.required_successor: For version 0.1.0, keep uncertain intents pending operator or test-harness reconciliation unless a separately reviewed status operation is added and pinned. Do not infer success from a sent byte, timeout, lease expiry or caller-created receipt. State how an authorised same-key replay is distinguished from forbidden blind retry, or leave replay unsupported in this version.

findings.finding: The source stores provider accepted_at in Todo.reminder_sent_at. TIME-D22 requires an explicit trust disposition before provider time becomes application authority; the service plan validates syntax but does not state that disposition.
findings.required_successor: Specify whether reminder_sent_at is a provider acceptance instant or a host observation time. If provider time remains authoritative, constrain its plausible range and prove the exact-key receipt was accepted before storing it; otherwise use a compiler-owned observation time while retaining accepted_at as provider evidence.

ready_parts: The local reference server is intentionally a real HTTP boundary; the in-process fake is kept separate.
The OpenAPI snapshot's version 0.1.0 and exact bytes match the candidate pin; the closed request, response and four named failure codes are reviewable.
The candidate matrix correctly separates proved no-effect pre-dispatch refusal from post-dispatch uncertainty and prohibits blind retry.
The intended egress and secret constraints exclude dynamic hosts, redirects, proxies and secret disclosure.
review_gate: Re-review the revised successor declaration, acceptance, case catalog and service plan for these six findings before RM-301 is approved or RM-302 starts. This review does not certify an implementation or executable HTTP conformance.

correction_re_review.scope: Independent semantic contract re-review only; no claim of executable HTTP, durable job, compiler, or full P10R conformance.

original_finding_dispositions.assessment: The successor uses a private generated nominal UUID per schedule revision, persists immutable payload before HTTP, reuses the same ID for permitted retries and binds JOB-001 to it. The human-owned pressure source and policy bytes remain comparison evidence; the narrow policy identity amendment is explicit.

Proved pre-dispatch no-effect failures are retryable within a shared budget; possible-dispatch timeout/loss/bad acknowledgement becomes durable unknown. The blanket timeout mapping has a compile-fail candidate.

Unique transactional intent creation, revision-aware admission, durable possible_dispatch before HTTP, revision-guarded completion, and held B while A is unknown cover duplicate workers, patch races, crash recovery and ABA revisions.

The bearer secret is confined to Authorization; the persisted UUID must match request body and generated header before dispatch, and the 202 echo must match before receipt construction. Exact import version, digest and single operation remain pinned.

The contract now explicitly says the pinned POST-only provider has no status lookup or automatic unknown replay. Unknown persists pending trusted host/operator evidence; the isolated reference harness may inspect its own stored receipt without pretending this is a production API.
Provider accepted_at is validated evidence only; a compiler-observed instant marks the matching current revision, independent of provider clock order or plausibility.

new_findings.finding: The initial correction candidate recorded retry:false on a two-attempt trace after a 429, while the single-429 case used retry:true for eligibility.
new_findings.resolution: The final catalog defines retry as eligibility at any intermediate injected failure, sets this trace to retry:true, and gives its successful terminal outcome final_retry:false. The 429 trace remains retry:true. These are now consistent.

correction_re_review.implementation_readiness: The revised semantic SERVICE-001 contract is sufficient for an RM-301 contract freeze under the owner's accepted reminder-identity decision. Exact parser spelling and stable diagnostics are RM-302 work; executable HTTP and durable job traces are RM-303/RM-305/RM-108 work. This review does not certify those implementations or the full P10R golden case gate.
